relations.evidence: The cbq shell executable, `cbq`, is available in the Couchbase Server installation directory. It is also available in the [Couchbase Server tools](../../cli/cli-intro.md#server-tools-packages) package beginning with version 7.6.2.

relations.subject: tool:cbq-shell
relations.evidence: The cbq shell supports the `http://`, `https://`, `couchbase://` and `couchbases://` protocol schemes. The `https://` and `couchbases://` protocol schemes are encrypted.

relations.subject: cbq:encrypted-connection
relations.evidence: You can connect to the cluster or node with an encrypted protocol scheme — that is, either `https://` or `couchbases://`. To do this, you can provide the root CA certificate, the chain certificate, and the client key file using the [\--cacert](#opt-cacert), [\--cert](#opt-cert), and [\--key](#opt-key) options.

relations.subject: cbq:opt-no-ssl-verify
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - mustUseInsteadWhen; --no-ssl-verify is the alternative to supplying certificates
relations.evidence: You can use the [\--no-ssl-verify](#opt-skip-verify) option to skip the verification of certificates.

relations.subject: cbq:encrypted-connection
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - doesNotSatisfy; records that the port cannot be specified for the two couchbase* schemes even though it can for http/https, i.e. one member of the enum does not accept an option the others do
relations.evidence:
You may optionally specify the port when using the `http://` or `https://` protocol schemes. When connecting to the query service, use the query port 8093, or 18093 for an encrypted connection. When connecting to the cluster, you don't need to specify the port as the connection uses round robin to find a query service to connect to. If you want to specify a port, use the admin port 8091, or 18091 for an encrypted connection.

You cannot specify the port when using the `couchbase://` or `couchbases://` protocol schemes.

relations.subject: tool:cbq-shell
relations.evidence: The host may be the IP address or hostname of any node in the cluster, as cbq will automatically discover the query nodes.

notable_absence.finding: The Server cbq page names no RBAC privilege, no role and no edition anywhere in 1,177 lines. Its entire access model is 'a user name and a password' - and unlike the Capella twin it does not even have a Prerequisites section stating that credentials must be created first. This is doubly notable because the page documents a capability with clear authorization semantics (multiple credentials, each granting access to a different keyspace: 'alternative credentials with access to a second keyspace') without ever naming what grants that access. Compare monitoring-n1ql-query.md in this same batch, which does name the required role. Secondly, there is no registry predicate for 'credential grants access to a keyspace' - grantsChannelAccess is Sync Gateway channel vocabulary and inheritsAccessFromRole is about role inheritance; reconciliation may want grantsKeyspaceAccess.

cross_component_finding: The page carefully distinguishes THREE version strings that all look alike: the shell's own version ('SHELL VERSION : 7.6.2-3721'), the Go runtime version ('GO VERSION : go1.22.2'), and the query engine version returned by VERSION()/MIN_VERSION() - and it explicitly states the third is not the same as the Couchbase Server version ('this is not the same as the version of Couchbase Server itself'). That is four distinct version-bearing entities in one tool page. Any version: namespace in the registry must therefore be able to say WHAT is versioned, not just the number: version:server-8-0, version:cbq-shell-7-6-2 and version:query-engine-* are not interchangeable, and the existing flat pattern (version:server-7-0, version:sdk-3-3-0, version:cbl-3-3-0) already encodes the subject in the id, which is the right instinct and should be kept.
cross_product_finding: 162 changed lines, and almost all of them are the same three substitutions repeated - but two are genuine capability differences that should be recorded as identity-distinguishing, not merged. (1) MULTIPLE CREDENTIALS ACTUALLY WORK ON SERVER AND NOT ON CAPELLA. Server: 'To specify multiple credentials, append all the user names and passwords to the same credentials array' and the option table gives './cbq -c=$USER:$PASSWORD,$USER2:$PASSWORD2'. Capella: 'if you specify multiple credentials, Couchbase Capella only recognizes the first credential' and 'If you specify more than one credential with this option, Couchbase Capella only uses the first one'. The section is even retitled - Server 'Providing Multiple Credentials for Authorization' vs Capella 'Switching Between Credentials'. This is a real behavioural divergence on the same flag of the same tool and is the best disablesFeatureFor / behavesDifferentlyUnder candidate in the batch; no relation was asserted because the Server page contains no quote about Capella. (2) PROTOCOL SCHEME. Server supports four schemes with optional ports; Capella permits exactly one ('To connect to Couchbase Capella, you must use the `couchbases://` protocol scheme') and adds mandatory --cacert plus -skip-verify to every single example. Capella also states that the default 'http://localhost:8091' 'does not enable you to connect to Couchbase Capella'. (3) Capella has a Prerequisites section (tools download, connection string, cluster access credentials, allowed IP address, security certificate) with no Server counterpart - the Server page simply assumes a local install. (4) Section retitling tracks the platform model throughout: 'Connecting to the Cluster or Query Node' vs 'Connecting to the Cluster'; 'Server and Shell Information' vs 'Cluster and Shell Information'. DOCUMENTATION DEFECTS, Server-side only, both in the -e/--engine flag: line 293 renders './cbq --e $BASE_URL -u $USER -p $PASSWORD' (double hyphen with the single-letter form) and line 357 renders './cbq e $BASE_URL -c=$USER:$PASSWORD,$USER2:$PASSWORD2' (hyphen missing entirely). The Capella page has '-e' correctly in both places, so these are regressions introduced in the Server variant.
version_finding: Three findings. (1) The availableSince claim is real but narrower on Server than the shared id suggests. The Capella record asserted tool:cbq-shell availableSince command-line-tools-package:7.6.2 from 'available in the Couchbase command line tools package beginning with version 7.6.2'. The Server page says cbq 'is available in the Couchbase Server installation directory' AND 'is also available in the Couchbase Server tools package beginning with version 7.6.2'. So on Server the tool itself has no version gate at all - only the standalone redistributable does - whereas on Capella the package IS the only way to get it, making the same sentence a hard prerequisite there and a convenience note here. Reconciliation should attach availableSince to the package, not to the tool, and note that the two products even call the package different things ('Couchbase Server tools' vs 'command line tools'). (2) Internal version inconsistency on an 8.0 page: the prose Version section shows 'GO VERSION : go1.22.2 / SHELL VERSION : 7.6.2-3721' while the two reference tables at the bottom of the same page show 'GO VERSION : go1.21.6 / SHELL VERSION : 7.6.0-2176'. Neither is an 8.0 build. A reader cannot tell which shell version the 8.0 docs describe. The Capella page carries the identical inconsistency, so it is inherited from shared source rather than introduced here. (3) No deprecation vocabulary at all: 1,177 lines documenting roughly 40 command line options and 30 shell commands, and not one is marked deprecated, superseded or renamed - even though the option table lists both '-skip-verify' (used throughout the Capella examples) and '--no-ssl-verify' (the name used in the Server prose) without saying whether one supersedes the other. That unexplained pair is the closest thing to a renamedFrom candidate on the page, and it is unresolvable from the text.
